key_insight: PINN training can match full-space performance within a small Hessian eigensubspace selected by gradient alignment rather than curvature magnitude.
engineering_relevance: Gradient-aligned subspaces could guide more efficient optimizers for PDE-solving neural networks facing severely ill-conditioned loss landscapes.
method: Select the dominant aligned subspace (DAS) by gradient alignment, not eigenvalue magnitude.
Train within DAS using line search and extend the analysis to Gauss–Newton.
evidence_signal: Across Poisson, heat, wave, and viscous Burgers benchmarks, DAS-restricted training empirically matches full-space training even when the projected Hessian remains ill-conditioned.
watch_item: Full Hessian eigendecomposition is costly at scale; the abstract does not establish end-to-end computational savings.
paper_title: A Systematic Analysis of a Small Optimal Subspace for Physics-Informed Neural Networks: $n$-DAS $\subset \mathbb{R}^p$
